messages:
maria: Heads-up — quick sync on messaging for next week's webinar + inbound routing. We need sharp, testable claims for the webinar hero and a simple routing map so signups flow into the right SDR/AE queues. I pushed a draft here: https://docs.google.com/xxx (please don't edit until I consolidate).

alex: Got the doc, skimmed. Two immediate asks: 1) name-checking competitors — avoid direct vendor comparisons unless we have bench review signoff; 2) landing page hero needs a one-liner and a supporting metric.

jonah: Bench quick note from infra: the internal perf run shows ~45% tail latency improvement (95p) vs our previous config for the same model under synthetic burst. Cost-per-1k-tokens improved ~27% after batching + KV cache. 

sara: Nice. For the webinar hooks I'd A/B test these two headlines: 
- Option A: "Predictable LLM inference — <lower cost>, <low tail latency>"
- Option B: "Ship LLM features with production SLAs, not guesswork"
We should put one metric in the subhead (either cost or 95p latency).

maria: I like A and B. But keep the language customer-facing: 'predictable' and 'SLAs' resonate with mid-market and platform teams. Also, sales wants a short competitive play for the follow-up email.

alex: Routing rules draft (very small snippet):
```
if form.source == "webinar_signup":
  route_team = "SDR-webinar"
  tag = "webinar:precision-routing"
else if form.question contains "infra" or "deployment":
  route_team = "Solutions-Infra"
```
This is what ops can implement in the form handler.

jonah: On benchmark phrasing — legal/compliance note: don't publish the raw percent comparisons without context. Suggest: "Benchmarks show material reductions in tail latency and token cost with Redwood's routing + caching — contact us for repo and methodology." Then have a locked appendix for field teams.

sara: For sales one-liners (2 options):
- "Unified runtime for consistent latency and predictable unit economics."
- "Move from model experiments to production with rollout controls and cost guardrails."
Which reads better for follow-up?

maria: Both are good. I'll slot the first into the email opener, second into the one-pager.

alex: Small ask: can eng produce a 1-paragraph explainer of the test methodology? Sales wants to cite something concise when prospects ask.

jonah: I'll draft a paragraph by tomorrow AM. It'll mention dataset (internal replay), model family, hardware, and the fact results are workload-dependent.

opsbot: Reminder: webinar assets due EOD Wednesday — slides, landing page copy, and battlecard one-pager.

maria: Last operational items:
- Legal review on any % claims (alex to submit)
- Finalize landing hero by Tue EOD (sara + maria)
- Routing rules to staging by Wed AM (alex + eng-infra)
- One-pager for SDRs with two rebut lines vs managed endpoints (maria to own)

alex: I'll open the legal ticket now. Also will drop the routing snippet into the form handler PR once we confirm tags.

maria: Thanks all. Goal: lock messaging by Tue so we can run A/B test Wednesday and have routing live before email send. :rocket:
